title: Stop checkout hooks from executing branch-controlled code or overwriting user hooks
description:
## Finding

Entering the development shell installs a host-side `post-checkout` hook that later executes a script from whichever branch/worktree has just been checked out. A hostile branch can therefore gain host code execution merely by being checked out, before any sandbox/trust admission. The installer also overwrites an existing hook, and the hook overwrites user-managed pre-commit configuration in linked worktrees.

## Evidence

* `flake.nix:456-480` runs automatically on non-CI dev-shell entry, resolves the effective `core.hooksPath`, and unconditionally runs `install ... "$hooks_dir/post-checkout"`. It has no ownership marker, collision policy, composition, no-follow validation, or atomic generation fence. A global/shared `core.hooksPath` can affect unrelated repositories.
* The installed `test/git-hooks/post-checkout.sh:21-31` runs after checkout and executes `sh test/git-hooks/heal-worktree.sh` by a relative path in the *newly checked-out tree*. The branch being inspected controls those bytes.
* The delegated healer directly rewrites shared `.git/config` at `test/git-hooks/heal-worktree.sh:73-112`; its safety/race deficiencies overlap <issue id="170ba4b4-3f08-4ec4-8d80-c14cdc8da795" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-371/make-git-config-self-healing-no-follow-atomic-and-race-safe">THE-371</issue>, but here the more fundamental problem is that an untrusted branch chooses the program.
* `post-checkout.sh:35-47` claims a real file is an already-live configuration, but the condition accepts only a live symlink. In a linked worktree, `ln -sf "$src" "$cfg"` replaces an existing regular `.pre-commit-config.yaml` or foreign/dangling symlink without ownership proof.
* The hook intentionally lives in the common hooks directory and therefore runs for every linked worktree, exactly where branch trust differs.

## Impact

Checking out or creating a worktree for an untrusted pull request can execute arbitrary branch-controlled shell with the developer's host filesystem, credentials, signing agents, network, and repository authority. This bypasses the product's sandbox decision before an agent is launched. Ordinary use can also destroy a user's existing `post-checkout` hook or per-worktree pre-commit configuration and can persist Thegn behavior into unrelated repositories through a global hooks path.

## Required remediation

Remove all execution of scripts resolved from the post-checkout worktree. Any installed hook component must be immutable/trusted, address the intended repository by verified identity, and compose with rather than replace foreign hooks. Prefer eliminating automatic Git-hook installation in favor of an explicit repository-scoped setup command or a trusted hook multiplexer with provenance.

The worktree config seeding operation must refuse foreign collisions, never replace a regular file/directory/symlink it does not own, and use rooted no-follow, atomic operations with a clear recovery path. Shared Git-config repair must use the generation-fenced primitive owned by <issue id="170ba4b4-3f08-4ec4-8d80-c14cdc8da795" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-371/make-git-config-self-healing-no-follow-atomic-and-race-safe">THE-371</issue>, not an unchecked branch script.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Checking out a branch that replaces `test/git-hooks/post-checkout.sh`, `heal-worktree.sh`, config files, or similarly named paths cannot execute any bytes from that branch.
- [ ] Dev-shell entry never overwrites a foreign `post-checkout` hook or a global/shared hooks directory without explicit scoped consent and recoverable composition.
- [ ] A regular, directory, valid foreign symlink, dangling symlink, and racing replacement at `.pre-commit-config.yaml` are preserved and reported; only a positively owned artifact may be refreshed.
- [ ] Installed hook identity is immutable/versioned and repository-scoped; execution verifies the exact repository/common-dir authority and does not act on an unrelated repo.
- [ ] Hook install/update/uninstall is transactional, no-follow, ownership-aware, and restores prior state on failure.
- [ ] Tests create a malicious branch whose post-checkout paths write a sentinel and prove checkout/worktree creation never triggers it.
- [ ] Tests cover repository-local and global `core.hooksPath`, an existing executable hook, multiple worktrees, concurrent shell entry/checkout, symlinked parents/leaves, interrupted update, uninstall, and rollback.
- [ ] No hook path silently swallows a security-relevant collision or failed repair.
- [ ] Documentation clearly distinguishes optional local developer gates from trusted CI/merge enforcement and never treats a mutable checkout hook as a security boundary.

## Dependency mapping

Dependency-ready. Directly blocks <issue id="49c93a3f-a87b-4654-a598-28e990d5a94b" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-197/restore-enforceable-pushpr-ci-coverage-for-high-risk-changes">THE-197</issue> because push/PR enforcement cannot rely on a development workflow that obtains host execution from the candidate branch and may replace user hooks. Related to <issue id="1b0f9f75-b333-495c-86d8-b5bd273087d4" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-225/fence-sandbox-git-writes-from-hooks-and-host-executed-control-metadata">THE-225</issue> (sandbox-to-host Git hook persistence), <issue id="170ba4b4-3f08-4ec4-8d80-c14cdc8da795" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-371/make-git-config-self-healing-no-follow-atomic-and-race-safe">THE-371</issue> (safe Git config repair), <issue id="f233a03a-c754-40a8-b1d3-ae3f2318240c" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-418/never-auto-approve-or-host-execute-repository-direnv-code-during">THE-418</issue> (pre-sandbox host execution of repository code), and <issue id="8891e03a-1be5-45fb-b0e1-6169ec8ff0f7" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-415/make-source-installation-ownership-aware-no-follow-and-transactional">THE-415</issue> (ownership-aware transactional installation).
